overall_assessment: MIXED — hold the TQA gate. This was a bounded static review of the eight frozen paths plus necessary public BFF/DI/filter/runner callers; no test, runtime, provider, network, Git, or file-write action was performed. The dispatch reports API lint/build plus 141 unit and 288 real-PostgreSQL tests green, and Web build plus 28 unit tests green; those are accepted as supplied evidence, not rerun evidence. Browser was pending at dispatch and is not credited as passed. Product-contract alignment is otherwise strong: the shared convergence helper retains exact attempt/generation/epoch identity, avoids a version bump for an already-complete attempt, and the official caller deliberately uses null epoch while unofficial paths retain numeric epoch checks. The production Meta adapter genuinely bounds itself to one grant/debug request and at most two phone pages, uses the fixed Graph host, opaque bounded cursors, scoped authorization, and redirect rejection; the unit tests exercise the real adapter through a fetch seam and assert the three-call cap, host, auth, cursor, grant, exhaustion, cycle, and oversize cases. The Nest/BFF/CSRF/DI/real-PG E2E tests add meaningful business assertions rather than count-only checks: repeated official verify preserves attempt/version/credential/identity/receipt, while unofficial recovery and stale-generation/epoch/null-epoch cases cover positive and rollback behavior. This layering is efficient: the E2E fake is appropriately not misrepresented as real Graph HTTP, and its page-call counter is not used as proof of the adapter's total HTTP budget. Static bypass review found no focused/skipped test, test-only production route, or broad production fallback in the reviewed delta. Fail-first evidence is limited but honestly bounded: prior cp36/cp36b functional RED supports the recovered behavior, while the added method has documented test-after debt because a method-not-found RED would have established scaffolding rather than product behavior. Security framing is good for fixed-host/scoped-token handling and no sensitive response assertion was weakened. Performance is statically acceptable: three serial requests at ten seconds each remain within the 45-second lease, and the extra convergence lookup is an exact-key miss path. The material gap is the required safe META_INDISPONIVEL failure contract at the public BFF boundary; it is neither visibly translated nor proven end-to-end. Decision adherence is otherwise consistent with D-03/D-04/D-06/D-07, subject to that error-boundary gap and the explicitly pending browser/platform evidence.
recommended_path: Recommended path: resolve TQA-CP36C-01 before accepting this delta. Option A (recommended): introduce a narrow, approved translation from MetaIndisponivelError to the project’s controlled HTTP error catalog with code META_INDISPONIVEL, then add one real Nest/BFF/CSRF/Prisma regression that drives an inconclusive second-page result through DI and asserts the public status/code plus unchanged channel, attempt/version, credential, identity, and receipt. Option B: use a narrowly scoped exception filter if the approved architecture intends the same mapping for all Meta callers; prove its registration in the Test AppModule wiring. Option C: explicitly change the approved contract to a generic internal error; this is not recommended because it discards the stated safe-inconclusive catalog behavior. In either A or B, assert error.code as well as the error class in adapter tests, align the browser fixture’s failure representation with the chosen boundary behavior, and record the source-owned Windows Docker browser result separately. Do not convert the dispatch’s pending browser state, or outstanding live-provider evidence, into a passing claim.

findings.title: META_INDISPONIVEL is not proven or visibly translated at the BFF boundary
findings.rationale: Counterexample: an otherwise valid scoped grant whose first and second phone pages omit the selected number while the second page advertises another cursor reaches MetaIndisponivelError in api-app/src/integrations/meta/meta.client.ts:150-153. That type is a plain Error with a code field at :33-35; ChannelsService awaits it directly at api-app/src/domain/channels/channels.service.ts:281-290, the BFF controller returns that service call directly at api-app/src/surfaces/bff/channels.controller.ts:84-92, and AppModule registers only the Prisma-specific filter at api-app/src/app.module.ts:32-40. It therefore reaches Nest’s unknown-error path rather than a demonstrated controlled META_INDISPONIVEL response. The new adapter tests assert instance type and request counts at api-app/src/integrations/meta/meta.client.spec.ts:173-193, but not error.code or HTTP translation; the real BFF/PG E2E covers only successful repeated verify at api-app/test/number-onboarding-flow.e2e-spec.ts:89-106. The browser fixture also throws a generic Error for this branch at api-app/test/browser-server.cjs:83-97. Why now: cp36c newly makes bounded pagination failure reachable from persisted official admin verify and explicitly specifies safe inconclusive META_INDISPONIVEL behavior. Assertion efficacy is consequently incomplete despite otherwise strong state assertions; one targeted BFF/PG negative would close it efficiently without broadening the suite.
findings.suggested_action: A (recommended): map MetaIndisponivelError at the approved BFF/service boundary to the controlled META_INDISPONIVEL HTTP contract and add a real Nest/BFF/CSRF/Prisma negative asserting status, code, and no mutation of channel/attempt/version/credential/identity/receipt. B: register a narrow shared exception filter and prove the same behavior through AppModule. C: retain generic Error/500 only after an explicit contract decision; do not treat the current class-only unit assertions as proof of the required public behavior.

findings.title: Browser-fixture parity and browser-platform evidence remain unclosed
findings.rationale: Counterexample: the modified browser fixture implements its own bounded lookup but represents an inconclusive result as generic Error rather than MetaIndisponivelError at api-app/test/browser-server.cjs:83-97. A browser journey could therefore exercise a failure representation different from the real adapter, especially after the public error mapping is corrected. Separately, the bounded package records the browser gate as running/pending, not passed, at foundation_documentation/artifacts/reviews/leadshug-number-onboarding-20261015/evidence/cp36c-tqa-package.md:17. Why now: cp36c changes that fixture and the medium-critical journey is explicitly Windows Docker/browser-sensitive. This is an evidence and fixture-fidelity gap, not a claim that the browser leg failed; the source-owned runner documents the intended Windows Docker/Node 22/OpenSSL 3/PostgreSQL 16 matrix but does not itself prove execution.
findings.suggested_action: After closing TQA-CP36C-01, make the browser fixture express the same controlled failure contract or explicitly limit it to success-only coverage, then record the browser result from the source-owned Windows Docker lane separately. Do not backfill a pass from API/Web counts or from fixture-page call counters.
